Configuration moved into one build block. Editable in the CI Index Builder.

text.title: CI Index
text.sub: Configuration Management · CI Index Template Rev C draft · Tool rev B draft
text.lede: One record per Configuration Item. The index flags what applies to each CI and points to the record that owns each answer. It does not copy content from those records. The tool checks every row as you work and shows what needs review.
foot: **Reference.** CI Identification Process Rev I draft, the records and outputs section. CI Index Template Rev C draft.
This tool is a working aid. The index of record is maintained current in the CSA system for the program life.
Nothing is stored in the browser. Save the index to a file before you close the tab. The saved file keeps the edit log. An Excel export does not.

cols.help: Derived from Parent CI ID. 0 is the top-level CI.
Program-unique identifier for the CI. It is not the PIN. Renaming a CI ID updates every parent, variant, and supersession reference to it.
Every CI except the top-level CI names a parent that exists in the index. The tool derives Level and the name indentation from the parent, so the three forms of hierarchy always agree.
Nomenclature for the CI. Enter it without indentation. The export indents it two spaces per level.
HWCI, CSCI, or Firmware. Computer software is designated as CIs (CSCIs).

Who baselines and controls the CI’s specification. Acquirer-spec controlled: the CI has its own specification, which the Acquirer baselines and controls. Company-spec controlled: the CI sits below an Acquirer-spec controlled CI. The company baselines and controls its specification, where it has one. A change with Class I effect reaches the Acquirer through the parent CI’s baselines. GFE: government furnished and installed in the product structure. The Government holds its definition.
The design activity that owns the CI’s design.
CAGE code of the design activity. CAGE and PIN together form the full identification.

Part or identifying number per design activity convention. PIN is not unique across rows. One PIN may map to more than one CI. One CI may carry several PIN variants. Keep the base or representative PIN here.
PIN of the next higher assembly the CI installs into. Where the CI trees directly to the end item, enter the end item’s PIN. Enter N/A only where the CI has no higher assembly.
Number of instances of this PIN in the next higher assembly, from that assembly’s parts list. Enter N/A where NH PIN is N/A. Above 1, run Decision Path B of the same-CI decision aid.
The CI’s specification. A vendor item control drawing goes here, not in SCD.
The source control drawing, for an item whose internals the supplier designs while the company controls form, fit, function, interface, and qualification.

The interface control documents that define this CI’s interfaces, including interface requirements specifications and interface design descriptions. Separate entries with semicolons. They must match the interface register.
The supplier statement of work that flows CM requirements to the supplier. The classification log holds the work type and the designation authorship case.
The model element the CI resolves to, where MBSE is used.
The ATA chapter or S1000D SNS reference.
Leave blank where the CI resolves to a model element. Where the CI structure departs from the model, record the reason Systems Engineering accepted.

Criterion (b): failure might result in serious injury, loss of life, or loss of primary system capability. Record the answer from the CI selection criteria checklist. Before recording N, check the SCI sources and the unit record sources. Neither check catches an item whose loss is loss of primary system capability with no injury pathway. Find those items in the program’s own decomposition.

Safety-Critical Item: a hardware or software item that has been determined through analysis to potentially contribute to a hazard with Catastrophic or Critical mishap potential, or that may be implemented to mitigate a hazard with Catastrophic or Critical mishap potential. Before recording N, examine the FMEA or FMECA, the SMS hazard log, and the system safety hazard analysis reports. A FMECA criticality code names a failure mode, not an item.
The FMEA, FMECA, SMS hazard log entry, or system safety hazard analysis report that names the item. Blank where SCI = N.
The completed CI selection criteria checklist. The rationale lives on that checklist, not in this index.
The latest submittal and concurrence that cover this CI. Update it on resubmittal. GFE rows read N/A.
The FBL is a system-level baseline. Record it on the top-level CI only. Enter N/A (system-level baseline) on every other row.
Status or establishment date. For example: Established 2026-03-14, Planned CDR, or Internal, 2026-04-10.
The initial product baseline is established at completion of CDR.
Takes its event from the CI’s Audit Designation Assessment Record. For a CI designated for PCA, the event is PCA completion. Otherwise, it is no later than first production unit delivery.
Whether the product definition data requires serial number recording. Software CIs read N.
Whether the product definition data requires lot or batch recording. Both flags can be Y.

Every source that drives serial or lot/batch recording. Sources stack. Name the designation, not only the mechanism. A critical safety item gets its serial number through IUID, so pick Critical safety item, and add IUID only where IUID also applies on its own. Leave blank where no unit record is required.
The category of life limit only. The limit value stays in the product definition data. The recording flags come from the sources, not from the clock.
Y where the product definition data imposes controlled handling, packaging, or storage to keep the item conforming. Special handling is not a criticality designation and not a serialization driver.
Y where item unique identification applies to the CI. The identifier registers carry the unique item identifiers, not this index.
Y where the CI is a supplier-designed item procured as a unit, such as a vendor item or a supplier-designed assembly. The company does not decompose it into further CIs.
A CI reads Proposed until the Acquirer concurs. Rows are not deleted once concurred. De-designate the CI, or supersede it by a split or a consolidation.
For a split or a consolidation. The old row names the new CI IDs. Each new row names the old CI ID. Separate IDs with semicolons.
Short notes. Point to the owning record rather than copying its content.

reference.title: What this index is
items: The index holds CIs, and only CIs. Customer equipment outside the product structure goes on the interface register only. CIs that exist only between a sub-supplier and the company stay out. End-item traceability is not an index topic.
The index is the hub for CI status. It flags what applies to each CI and points to the record that owns each answer. It does not copy content from those records.
Each column holds a fixed property of the CI. Timing lives in the baseline columns.

reference.title: Definitions
items: **Configuration Item (CI).** Any hardware, software, firmware, or aggregation thereof that satisfies a system end-use function and is designated for separate configuration management. Designation includes establishing the CI’s requirements and verifying that its configuration meets those requirements and that its configuration documentation accurately describes its configuration.

**Part or Identifying Number (PIN).** The identifier that, combined with the design activity CAGE code, uniquely identifies an item and its configuration. The PIN changes when a modification creates a non-interchangeable condition.

**Safety-Critical Item (SCI).** A hardware or software item that has been determined through analysis to potentially contribute to a hazard with Catastrophic or Critical mishap potential, or that may be implemented to mitigate a hazard with Catastrophic or Critical mishap potential.
**Control Tier.** The record of who baselines and controls a CI’s specification. The three tiers are Acquirer-spec controlled, Company-spec controlled, and GFE.
**Product Definition Data (PDD).** The design data that defines an item’s physical and functional attributes: drawings, models, and associated lists such as parts lists.
The safety-critical item is not the critical safety item. Different authority, different object, different obligation.

reference.title: How the tool works
items: **Hierarchy is entered once.** Pick the parent. The tool derives Level and the indented name. The three forms of hierarchy in the workbook can no longer disagree.
**Checks run as you type.** They mark a cell for review. They never block entry. The Checks tab lists every finding and the rule behind it.
**Sources drive the flags.** Pick each source that drives the unit record. The tool shows what the sources call for, and sets the four flags on request.
**Rows are retired, not deleted.** A CI the Acquirer has concurred in cannot be deleted. De-designate it, or split or consolidate it. The tool keeps the old row and writes the trace on both sides.
**Same PIN, another position.** Decision Path B can return separate CIs against one PIN. This action copies the row under a new CI ID. Key CSA on the CI and the installed position together.

**Save keeps everything.** The saved file holds the index, the variants, and the edit log. The Excel export is the exchange copy. Import reads a Rev C workbook or a prior export. It reads the CI Index and PN Variants sheets.

reference.title: Rules carried from the template
items: Every CI goes to the Acquirer for concurrence, including Company-spec controlled CIs. A CI reads Proposed until the Acquirer concurs. Enter the concurrence, then set Status to Active. GFE rows read N/A.

Criterion (b) Met is the umbrella safety column. Criterion (b) is mandatory for safety. Any condition in Table C-1 satisfies criterion (b) on its own. Neither the SCI sources nor Table C-1 catch an item whose loss is loss of primary system capability with no injury pathway. Find those items in the program’s own decomposition.
Influencing parts fail criterion (b) by their own definition but qualify on criterion (a). See the criticality designations appendix.

The FBL is a system-level baseline. Record it on the top-level CI only. The initial product baseline is established at completion of CDR. The formalized PBL takes its event from the Audit Designation Assessment Record. This index does not record audit designation.
Do not copy handling instructions, IUID triggers, unique item identifiers, life limit values, date codes, or heat-lot details into this index.
Where MBSE is used, CI parent-child relationships mirror the model decomposition. A same-CI verdict that mismatches the model is not entered until Systems Engineering dispositions it.
